stages.name: Loyal to Rome
stages.desc: Roman territory, Latin colonies and allies that kept faith with Rome

stages.name: Contested
stages.desc: Fought over: sieges, raids, rival armies, or loyal and rebel towns side by side

stages.name: Defected to Hannibal
stages.desc: Communities that broke with Rome and joined Carthage

stages.name: Hannibal's last refuge
stages.desc: The Bruttian lands where Hannibal held out after 207 BC

stages.name: Retaken by Rome
stages.desc: Defectors recaptured or surrendered, often punished harshly

states.name: Pesaro and Urbino
timeline: The Roman colony of Sena Gallica and the Ager Gallicus stay loyal
Hasdrubal's relief army is destroyed on the Metaurus
Italy is safe from a second Carthaginian army from Spain

states.name: Ancona
timeline: Picenum and Greek Ancona stay loyal

states.name: Macerata
timeline: The Picentes stay loyal to Rome

states.name: Fermo
timeline: The Latin colony of Firmum stays loyal

states.name: Ascoli Piceno
timeline: Asculum and southern Picenum, ravaged by Hannibal in 217, stay loyal

states.name: Teramo
timeline: The Praetutii and the colony of Hadria stay loyal

states.name: Pescara
timeline: The Vestini and Marrucini stay loyal

states.name: Chieti
timeline: The Frentani and Marrucini stay loyal
Claudius Nero's army hurries north along the coast road to the Metaurus

states.name: Campobasso
timeline: Bovianum's Pentri and the Frentani of Larinum stay loyal

states.name: Foggia
timeline: Arpi, Salapia and Herdonea go over to Hannibal; Luceria stays loyal
Fabius the younger retakes Arpi in a night attack in the rain
Hannibal destroys a Roman army at Herdonea
Salapia is betrayed to Marcellus; Hannibal razes Herdonea and moves its people south

states.name: Barletta-Andria-Trani
timeline: Canusium shelters the survivors of Cannae
Marcellus fights Hannibal for three days near Canusium

states.name: Bari
timeline: The Peucetian towns of the coast stay loyal

states.name: Brindisi
timeline: Brundisium, Rome's port for the east, holds firm
A Roman fleet at Brundisium guards against Philip V of Macedon, Hannibal's new ally

states.name: Lecce
timeline: The Sallentine towns of the heel stay loyal
Hannibal camps among the Sallentini and some of their towns go over
After Tarentum falls the Sallentine rebels surrender

states.name: Taranto
timeline: Greek Tarentum keeps its Roman garrison; Tarentine hostages are held in Rome
Young nobles let Hannibal in by night; the Roman garrison holds the citadel
Fabius retakes Tarentum by treachery and sells thirty thousand people into slavery

states.name: Matera
timeline: Metapontum and Heraclea keep Roman garrisons
Metapontum and Heraclea go over to Hannibal after Tarentum
Hannibal evacuates Metapontum and falls back into Bruttium

states.name: Cosenza
timeline: The Bruttians rise and join Hannibal; Consentia opens its gates
Greek Thurii goes over to Hannibal
Hannibal's last refuge: the forests of the Sila feed and hide his army
Consentia and Pandosia return to Rome

states.name: Crotone
timeline: Petelia refuses to join Hannibal and is besieged by the Bruttians
Petelia falls after a long siege; Croton is taken
Croton becomes Hannibal's main base
Hannibal sets up a bronze record of his deeds at the temple of Hera Lacinia
Hannibal sails for Africa from Croton; Bruttium submits to Rome

states.name: Catanzaro
timeline: Bruttian communities of the isthmus join Hannibal
The heart of Hannibal's last Bruttian redoubt
Bruttium submits to Rome after Hannibal leaves

states.name: Reggio Calabria
timeline: Greek Rhegium keeps faith with Rome
Locri goes over to Carthage; Rhegium holds out alone
Hannibal's surprise dash on Rhegium fails
Hannibal drives the Romans from the walls of Locri
Scipio takes Locri; his legate Pleminius plunders it and its temple

states.name: Vibo Valentia
timeline: Bruttian Hipponium and the Tyrrhenian coast join Hannibal
Hannibal's last refuge on the Tyrrhenian side
Bruttium submits to Rome after Hannibal leaves

states.name: Potenza
timeline: Most Lucanians join Hannibal; the Latin colony of Venusia stays loyal
Gracchus is ambushed and killed in Lucania
Marcellus is killed in an ambush near Venusia
Nero beats Hannibal at Grumentum; the Lucanians return to Rome

states.name: Salerno
timeline: Hannibal takes Nuceria, lets its people go and burns it
Centenius Penula's army is destroyed on the Silarus
The Volceians of the upper Sele valley return to Rome

states.name: Naples
timeline: Naples refuses Hannibal; Marcellus beats him off outside Nola
Hannibal tries Nola again and besieges Cumae in vain
A third attack on Nola fails
With Capua fallen, the Bay of Naples is secure

states.name: Caserta
timeline: Capua, Italy's second city, joins Hannibal; Atella and Calatia follow
Hannibal's army winters in Capua; Casilinum falls after a starving siege
Fabius retakes Casilinum; Cales and Suessa stay loyal
Three Roman armies ring Capua with a double line of earthworks
Capua surrenders; its leaders die, its land is confiscated, its self-government ended

states.name: Latina
timeline: The Latin colonies and old Volscian towns of the coast hold firm
Circeii and Setia are among twelve Latin colonies that refuse more men and money

states.name: Rome
timeline: Rome refuses to ransom the prisoners of Cannae and arms eight thousand slave volunteers
Hannibal camps on the Anio, three miles from the walls, then marches away

states.name: Viterbo
timeline: Southern Etruria stays loyal and feeds Rome's armies

states.name: Trapani
timeline: Lilybaeum and Drepana, Roman since 241 BC, guard the western tip of Sicily

states.name: Messina
timeline: Messana, Rome's bridgehead in Sicily, stays loyal
Scipio's army gathers in Sicily for the invasion of Africa

states.name: Palermo
timeline: Panormus and the Roman province hold firm

states.name: Agrigento
timeline: Agrigentum lies inside the Roman province
Himilco lands a Carthaginian army and takes Agrigentum
Muttines betrays Agrigentum to Laevinus; all Sicily is Roman

states.name: Caltanissetta
timeline: The towns of central Sicily lie in the Roman province
Inland Sicilian towns go over to Carthage
The Sicilian rebels surrender after Agrigentum falls

states.name: Ragusa
timeline: Camarina lies in the Roman province
The south-east is fought over during the siege of Syracuse
Roman control returns after Syracuse falls

states.name: Syracuse
timeline: Old King Hiero of Syracuse, Rome's ally, sends grain and gold after Cannae
Young Hieronymus allies with Carthage; after his murder Syracuse breaks with Rome
Marcellus besieges Syracuse; Archimedes' machines hold him off
Syracuse falls and is sacked; Archimedes is killed

states.name: Catania
timeline: Catana lies in the Roman province
Himilco and Marcellus manoeuvre across eastern Sicily
The east of Sicily is secure after Syracuse falls

states.name: Enna
timeline: Henna, the hilltop sanctuary of Demeter, has a Roman garrison
Fearing betrayal, the Roman garrison massacres the people of Henna
The massacre drives much of inland Sicily to Carthage
The interior surrenders to Laevinus

states.name: Benevento
timeline: The Caudine Samnites go over to Hannibal; the colony of Beneventum holds
Gracchus defeats Hanno outside Beneventum; his slave volunteers win their freedom
Fulvius Flaccus storms Hanno's grain camp near Beneventum
The Samnite rebels return to Rome

states.name: Rieti
timeline: The Sabine country, Roman citizens since 268 BC, stays loyal

states.name: Terni
timeline: Umbrian towns and the colony of Narnia stay loyal
Narnia is among the twelve Latin colonies that refuse further levies

states.name: Perugia
timeline: Umbria, scene of Trasimene the year before, stays loyal

states.name: Frosinone
timeline: Latin colonies of the Liris valley, Fregellae and Sora, stay loyal
Hannibal marches on Rome up the Latin Way; Fregellae breaks its bridges to slow him
The Liris valley is quiet again after Hannibal's withdrawal

states.name: Avellino
timeline: The Hirpini open Compsa to Hannibal and join him
The Hirpini surrender their Carthaginian garrisons to Rome

states.name: L'Aquila
timeline: Marsi, Paeligni and the colony of Alba Fucens stay loyal
Alba Fucens and Carseoli refuse further levies with ten other Latin colonies

states.name: Isernia
timeline: The Pentri Samnites and the Latin colony of Aesernia keep faith with Rome

events.title: Rome arms slaves
events.text: After Cannae, Rome refuses to ransom its captured soldiers and buys eight thousand slaves to fight as volunteers.

events.title: Capua defects
events.text: Capua joins Hannibal on its own terms: its own laws, its own magistrates, no Campanian forced to serve.

events.title: Compsa opens
events.text: The Hirpini hand Compsa to Hannibal, the first of the Samnite defections.

events.title: Nuceria burned
events.text: Hannibal starves Nuceria into surrender, lets its people leave and burns the town.

events.title: Nola holds
events.text: Marcellus sallies from Nola and drives off Hannibal's assault.

events.title: Petelia besieged
events.text: The small town of Petelia refuses to break with Rome and is besieged by the Bruttians.

events.title: Winter in Capua
events.text: Hannibal's army winters in Capua: later Romans claimed its luxuries ruined his men.

events.title: Casilinum falls
events.text: After a siege in which the defenders ate leather and roots, Casilinum surrenders.

events.title: Cumae resists
events.text: Gracchus surprises the Campanians at Hamae, and Hannibal fails to take Cumae.

events.title: Locri defects
events.text: Locri admits a Carthaginian garrison; Rhegium alone holds the toe of Italy for Rome.

events.title: Macedon allies
events.text: Philip V of Macedon makes a treaty with Hannibal; a Roman fleet watches from Brundisium.

events.title: Battle of Beneventum
events.text: Gracchus defeats Hanno; the slave volunteers who fought are given their freedom.

events.title: Syracuse turns
events.text: Hiero's grandson Hieronymus allies with Carthage; he is murdered within months.

events.title: Massacre at Henna
events.text: The Roman garrison kills the citizens of Henna to forestall a defection.

events.title: Arpi retaken
events.text: Fabius's son storms Arpi on a rainy night; its people return to Rome.

events.title: Archimedes' machines
events.text: Marcellus attacks Syracuse by land and sea; Archimedes' cranes and catapults repel him.

events.title: Agrigentum taken
events.text: A Carthaginian army under Himilco lands in Sicily and takes Agrigentum.

events.title: Tarentum betrayed
events.text: Nico and Philemenus let Hannibal into Tarentum by night; the citadel holds out.

events.title: Gracchus killed
events.text: The proconsul Gracchus is lured into an ambush in Lucania and killed.

events.title: Disaster on the Silarus
events.text: Centenius Penula's makeshift army is wiped out by Hannibal.

events.title: First Herdonea
events.text: Hannibal destroys the army of the praetor Gnaeus Fulvius Flaccus in Apulia.

events.title: Thurii and Metapontum
events.text: The Greek cities of the gulf follow Tarentum over to Hannibal.

events.title: Capua encircled
events.text: Three Roman armies dig a double ring of ditches and ramparts around Capua.

events.title: Syracuse falls
events.text: Marcellus takes Syracuse; in the sack a soldier kills Archimedes.

events.title: March on Rome
events.text: To draw the besiegers off Capua, Hannibal camps on the Anio and rides to the Colline Gate.

events.title: Capua surrenders
events.text: Capua's leaders take poison or are beheaded; the city loses its land and self-government.

events.title: Dash on Rhegium
events.text: Hannibal races south to surprise Rhegium, and fails.

events.title: Salapia betrayed
events.text: Salapia's leaders hand the town and its Numidian garrison to Marcellus.

events.title: Herdonea razed
events.text: Hannibal wins again at Herdonea, then burns the town and moves its people south.

events.title: Sicily lost
events.text: Agrigentum is betrayed to Laevinus; Carthage is driven out of Sicily.

events.title: Tarentum retaken
events.text: Fabius, consul for the fifth time, takes Tarentum by treachery; thirty thousand are enslaved.

events.title: Colonies refuse
events.text: Twelve of thirty Latin colonies say they have no more men or money to give.

events.title: Battle of Canusium
events.text: Marcellus fights Hannibal for three days near Canusium.

events.title: Marcellus killed
events.text: Both consuls ride into an ambush near Venusia; Marcellus dies on the spot.

events.title: Battle of Grumentum
events.text: Claudius Nero checks Hannibal in Lucania as he moves north.

events.title: The Metaurus
events.text: Hasdrubal's army from Spain is destroyed; his head is thrown into Hannibal's camp.

events.title: Retreat to Bruttium
events.text: Hannibal gives up Lucania and Metapontum and withdraws to the toe of Italy.

events.title: Locri retaken
events.text: Scipio takes Locri; his legate Pleminius loots the shrine of Persephone.

events.title: Hera Lacinia
events.text: Hannibal leaves a bronze tablet of his campaigns, in Punic and Greek, in the temple near Croton.

events.title: Scipio sails
events.text: Scipio's army leaves Lilybaeum for Africa.

events.title: Consentia returns
events.text: Consentia and Pandosia surrender to the consul Sempronius.

events.title: Hannibal sails home
events.text: Recalled to defend Carthage, Hannibal embarks at Croton after fifteen years in Italy.

chartNote: Share of the area of the provinces shown (today's boundaries, from Lazio and the Marche to Sicily), by the allegiance of most of each province's communities. A simplification: ancient Italy was a patchwork of cities and peoples, many provinces held loyal and rebel towns side by side, and some dates are disputed (Tarentum fell in the winter of 213/212 BC).
